mixed4b:431.real_s1: The unit responds mainly to the head-and-neck region of dogs and similar furry mammals (wolf, meerkat), most strongly when the head faces the camera, the neck/shoulder area beside the face is clearly visible, and the head and upper body fill a moderate share of the frame. It responds weakly to related things, possibly including collar-like clothing such as lab coats.
mixed4b:431.real_s2: The unit responds to furry mammal heads, mostly dogs, seen frontally at a moderate scale (head and upper body filling roughly a quarter to half of the image), with the neck/shoulder region beside the face and furry ears clearly visible. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals with similar head structure.
mixed4b:431.real_s3: The unit responds to the head and fore-body of furry mammals, mostly dogs, and is most active when the head faces the camera, is sharp and well lit, and has the furry neck/shoulder area beside the face clearly in view, with the head-and-upper-body filling a quarter to half of the frame. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals.
mixed4b:431.null_s1: The unit mainly responds to dogs (many breeds, plus dog-like canids such as the white wolf), and more weakly to other furry mammals such as meerkats. It is somewhat stronger when the whole animal sits in the frame at moderate size and medium lighting, rather than filling the photo as a close-up.
mixed4b:431.null_s2: The unit responds mainly to dogs, especially their furry heads, ears and neck/shoulder areas, and weakly to other furry mammals such as meerkats, wolves and small mammals. Within those classes it fires more when the animal is moderately sized, fully in the frame and evenly lit.
mixed4b:431.null_s3: The unit responds mainly to dogs, especially furry dog heads and fore-bodies, with weaker responses to other furry mammals and canid-like animals such as meerkats and wolves. Within its top classes it is somewhat more active when the dog is moderately sized, fully in frame, off-center (left) and in medium lighting, rather than when it is a large close-up.

mixed4b:443.real_s1: The unit responds to frontal, centered, upright furry-mammal faces with both eyes clearly visible, most strongly dog faces seen head-on. It extends to similar faces of other furry mammals (e.g., lesser panda, cats, bears), not only canids.
mixed4b:443.real_s2: Responds to frontal, centered canine faces with both eyes clearly visible, i.e. a dog looking straight at the camera, and extends weakly to other frontal furry mammal faces (e.g., lesser panda, cats).
mixed4b:443.real_s3: The unit responds to frontal, centered, single animal faces with both eyes visible, mainly dog faces, and extends more weakly to other furry mammal faces such as the lesser panda and probably foxes and wolves.
mixed4b:443.null_s1: The unit responds to dogs (across many breeds) and extends weakly to similar-looking furry animals such as the lesser panda. Within those classes it prefers a whole, moderately sized animal turned toward the right (three-quarter or side view) rather than a frontal close-up of the face.
mixed4b:443.null_s2: The unit responds to dogs across many breeds and weakly extends to dog-like furry mammals such as the lesser panda. Within those classes it prefers whole animals facing or turned toward the right (three-quarter view), not specifically upright faces or the eye region.
mixed4b:443.null_s3: The unit responds mainly to dogs across many breeds, with weaker extension to similar furry mammals such as the lesser panda. Within those classes it favors whole, uncropped animals turned sideways, especially facing right, not frontal eye-region close-ups.

mixed4b:429.real_s1: The unit responds to a clearly visible, upright, frontal dog face with eyes and nose/muzzle all in view, framed at a moderate size; breed, coat colour and fur texture do not matter.
mixed4b:429.real_s2: The unit responds to clearly visible, upright, roughly frontal dog faces where both eyes and the nose/muzzle are shown, regardless of breed, coat colour or fur texture.
mixed4b:429.real_s3: The unit responds to clearly visible, upright, frontal dog faces in which both eyes and the muzzle are seen sharply at moderate size. It does not care about breed, coat colour or fur texture.
mixed4b:429.null_s1: The unit responds to dog faces, especially large, close-up faces that are tilted or turned (three-quarter view) rather than upright and frontal, with a weaker preference for warm tan/golden coats and warm-tinted photos.
mixed4b:429.null_s2: The unit responds to dog faces, mainly close-up or prominent ones that are tilted or turned (three-quarter view) rather than strictly upright and frontal, with a modest preference for warm/tan tones.
mixed4b:429.null_s3: The unit responds to dog faces across many breeds. Within dog photos it prefers large, close-up faces whose head is tilted sideways or turned to a three-quarter view, not the upright, head-on faces the original explanation describes.

mixed4d:409.real_s1: The unit responds to a horizontally elongated body visibly raised on wheels or legs and seen lengthwise, chiefly cars and trucks in three-quarter or side view, possibly extending to standing quadrupeds with the same layout.
mixed4d:409.real_s2: The unit responds to a horizontally elongated body raised on wheels, seen from the side or three-quarter angle, mostly road vehicles. It is weak or silent for front or rear views and for bodies whose wheels are hidden. The proposed dog-torso half is not supported: all 12 top classes are vehicles (plus airliner and grille), and no animals appeared.
mixed4d:409.real_s3: The unit responds to a horizontally elongated body raised on wheels or legs, seen from the side or at an angle so its long flank and wheels/legs are visible: mostly cars and trucks, with standing four-legged animals (dogs, a weasel) as a weaker related case. The response is strongest for a sharp, well-framed three-quarter or side view, and weak for front/rear views or when the wheels are cropped out.
mixed4d:409.null_s1: The unit responds to road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks) seen from the side or three-quarter angle, where an elongated body sits on visible wheels, especially a partial side view that includes the front wheel. The claimed main preference for side-on standing dogs or quadrupeds is not supported, since vehicles dominate its most active classes.
mixed4d:409.null_s2: The unit mainly responds to the side body and front-wheel area of road vehicles, seen as a partial side view raised on wheels; the dog/quadruped torso is plausibly a related extension (an elongated body in profile raised on legs) rather than an unrelated second concept.
mixed4d:409.null_s3: The unit responds to the side of a horizontally elongated body raised on wheels or legs, mainly a road vehicle's flank seen from the side or three-quarter view with the front wheel in view, and more weakly the flank of a standing quadruped such as a dog.

mixed4b:237.real_s1: The unit responds to clearly visible side/door windows of real, intact road vehicles, especially the front cab or driver-door window with its frame and pillars, best seen in a three-quarter view.
mixed4b:237.real_s2: The unit responds to clearly visible side door windows of real, upright road vehicles, especially the front cab/driver door window with a well-defined frame and pillars, seen from a front or rear three-quarter view.
mixed4b:237.real_s3: The unit responds to the clearly visible side door-window of a real, upright road vehicle (framed glass pane with distinct pillars and door edge), especially the front cab/driver window seen in three-quarter view at medium scale. Its activity drops for toys or drawings, unusual angles, and blurry or obscured frames.
mixed4b:237.null_s1: The unit responds to side windows of road vehicles, meaning door glass panes with clearly defined frames and pillars, most strongly on cab or driver-door windows. It extends more weakly to rear passenger or cargo-area side windows and to toy or model vehicles that show the same window-frame structure.
mixed4b:237.null_s2: The unit responds to the side door window and its frame and pillars on road vehicles, mostly cabs of trucks and buses. Windshield-only views do not drive it.
mixed4b:237.null_s3: The unit responds to the clearly framed side window of a road vehicle, meaning a door window with sharply defined frame and pillars, most often the front cab/driver door window. It extends somewhat to rear or cargo side windows, larger vehicles (trucks, buses), and non-realistic or tilted renderings of vehicles.

mixed4b:373.real_s1: The unit responds to a clearly visible, medium-sized road-vehicle wheel sitting inside its wheel arch or fender, seen from the side or at an angle (not head-on), typically the front wheel of a van, bus, truck or similar vehicle.
mixed4b:373.real_s2: The unit detects a clearly visible, medium-sized road-vehicle wheel sitting inside its wheel arch, seen from the side or at an angle (not head-on), most strongly when it is a front wheel.
mixed4b:373.real_s3: The unit responds to a clearly visible, medium-sized vehicle wheel sitting inside its wheel arch, seen from the side or at an angle, most strongly a front wheel. It fires across vehicle types (cars, vans, buses, trucks).
mixed4b:373.null_s1: The unit responds to large road vehicles (vans, buses, trucks, cars) seen side-on and level, so their wheels look round and fully visible. The fender or arch around the wheel is not what drives it.
mixed4b:373.null_s2: The unit responds to a road vehicle seen side-on and level, with its wheel clearly visible and looking round. The wheel arch/fender part of the original description is not supported, and the upright-orientation claim could not be tested.
mixed4b:373.null_s3: The unit responds to a clearly visible, round vehicle wheel seen from the side, preferably the front wheel, on large road vehicles that fill the frame. The wheel arch or fender above it does not appear to be part of what it detects.

mixed4e:55.real_s1: The unit responds to a clearly visible, frontal, upright muzzle of a furry mammal (nose, whisker pad, mouth, often with a light-coloured muzzle and visible whiskers), centred in the frame, regardless of species. It responds weakly to face-like car fronts and grilles.
mixed4e:55.real_s2: The unit responds to a clearly visible, upright, front-facing muzzle region (nose, mouth, whisker pad) of a furry mammal, regardless of species. It gives weak responses to face-like fronts such as car grilles.
mixed4e:55.real_s3: The unit responds to a clearly visible, upright, front-facing muzzle of a furry mammal (nose, mouth and whisker pad, often with light fur and whiskers), centered and sharp in the frame. It responds more weakly to frontal face-like structures such as car grilles.
mixed4e:55.null_s1: The unit responds mainly to the lower face and muzzle region of furry mammals, especially foxes, red pandas and cats. It extends more weakly to face-like car fronts with grilles.
mixed4e:55.null_s2: The unit is mainly selective at the category level for small-to-medium furry mammals with fox/cat-like faces (lynx, cats, foxes, red panda, weasel, hamster, papillon). It extends fairly strongly to car fronts (grille, sports car, beach wagon), which fits a face-like-front pattern, but the claim that it specifically tracks the muzzle region is not supported.
mixed4e:55.null_s3: The unit mainly responds to furry mammal faces (wild and domestic cats, foxes, red pandas, weasels, hamsters, small dogs), with a weaker extension to car fronts with grilles. Within a class it seems to prefer heads that are moderately sized, partly hidden, tilted or slightly blurry, rather than sharp full-frame close-ups of the muzzle.

mixed5a:719.real_s1: The unit mainly responds to close-up views of man-made or handmade objects that fill the frame. It responds somewhat more when the image is a decorative or patterned surface, or an arrangement with no single centered subject, rather than one isolated object.
mixed5a:719.real_s2: The unit responds mainly to close-up, frame-filling views of compact man-made or crafted objects (wallets, erasers, sharpeners, stockings, shoes). It responds more strongly when the image is busy or ornamented, with decorative curved or radial patterns and no single clear main subject, rather than to a clean outline of one object.
mixed5a:719.real_s3: The unit responds mainly to close-up, frame-filling views of man-made or handmade objects, and more so when the frame shows a surface texture or ornamental pattern rather than one centered, sharply outlined subject. Radial or floral decorative motifs add somewhat to the response, but curved contours as such do not drive it.
mixed5a:719.null_s1: The unit responds to curved contours that form the outline of a man-made object, seen at moderate contrast against its background, rather than to decorative curved patterns. The proposed extension to radial or petal ornament is not supported.
mixed5a:719.null_s2: The unit responds mainly to the curved outline of a man-made object seen against a moderately contrasting background, and less to curves that are only decorative patterns on a surface. It may also respond to curved edges in general.
mixed5a:719.null_s3: Within its top classes (small man-made items like wallets, stockings, eraser, ocarina, loafer), the unit leans toward photos where a curved contour is an object outline seen with moderate rather than stark contrast against its background. It does not track ornamental radial or floral patterns, and the original 'curved shape' story is only weakly supported.
